plan.contextChunk: This figure is part of a worked example asking to evaluate the double integral of (2x - y^2) over the triangular region R enclosed between y = -x + 1, y = x + 1, and y = 3. The figure shows the triangular region R in the xy-plane with vertices at (-2, 3), (0, 1), and (2, 3); the bounding lines y = 3 (top), y = -x + 1 (lower left), and y = x + 1 (lower right) are labeled. The y-axis divides R into two sub-regions: R1 (shaded blue, left half) and R2 (shaded yellow, right half), each with a red vertical strip indicating the direction of inner integration. The figure illustrates the decomposition of R into two type-I sub-regions required when the lower boundary changes expression across the y-axis.

interactionPlan.concept: Decomposing a region of integration into sub-regions when the boundary formulas change under a chosen integration order.
elements: region R1 (shaded light blue, x in [-2, 0])
region R2 (shaded light orange, x in [0, 2])
vertical representative slice in R1 (red vertical segment)
vertical representative slice in R2 (red vertical segment)

interactions.teaches: how changing the order of integration determines whether the region must be split into sub-regions

interactions.label: Sweep Slice

demo_steps.title: The Triangular Region
demo_steps.narration: Observe the triangular region R bounded by y = 3, y = -x + 1, and y = x + 1. We want to set up a double integral over this region.

demo_steps.title: Type I: Splitting at x = 0
demo_steps.narration: Using vertical slices (dy dx), the lower boundary changes from y = -x + 1 to y = x + 1 at x = 0. Therefore, we must split the region into R1 and R2 and set up two separate integrals.

demo_steps.title: Type II: A Simpler Alternative
demo_steps.narration: Switch to horizontal slices (dx dy). Notice that the left boundary is always x = 1 - y and the right boundary is always x = y - 1. No splitting is required!

interactionPlan.keyInsight: Splitting a region of integration is necessary when a boundary curve is defined by different formulas over different parts of the domain; switching the order of integration can often simplify the calculation by avoiding this split.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: A Cartesian coordinate system with a triangular region. For Type I, shade R1 in light blue and R2 in light orange, separated by the y-axis, with a vertical red line representing the integration slice at the slider position. For Type II, shade the entire triangle in a single uniform color (e.g., light purple) and show a horizontal green/red line representing the integration slice. Label boundary equations clearly near their respective lines.
